protections: P1: data a namespaced policy (Policy / CleanupPolicy) pulls into its rule context through Kyverno's own credentials must stay inside the policy's namespace. Today the context loader factory throws the policy away (pkg/engine/factories/contextloaderfactory.go:21), so no loader can scope by namespace. Precedents in the same repo: CEL namespacedImpl (pkg/cel/libs/resource/namespaced_impl.go:27,93) and mutate targets (pkg/engine/handlers/mutation/load_targets.go:93-96).

evidence: pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:47 passes the raw urlPath straight to RawAbsPath without checking the namespace
pkg/clients/dclient/client.go:168 does GET RequestURI(path) using Kyverno's own rest client
pkg/engine/factories/contextloaderfactory.go:21 ignores the PolicyInterface argument (`_`), so the loader never knows the policy's namespace
pkg/validation/policy/validate.go:1411-1435 validateAPICall checks only Service/URLPath exclusivity and JMESPath syntax, not the namespace

traps.reason_to_dismiss: service calls are meant for external HTTP services, not the kube API, so a urlPath namespace check looks complete; any URL that points back at the API server reads like a separate SSRF concern
evidence: pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:148-152 adds Kyverno's own service-account bearer token whenever the policy sets no Authorization header
pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:159 reads that token from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:131 uses apiCall.Service.URL exactly as the policy wrote it, so it can name the API server and any namespace path

traps.reason_to_dismiss: configMap entries are a typed, non-secret lookup and differ from raw apiCall paths; the advisory talks about apiCall/RBAC, so a solver may treat ConfigMaps as low-sensitivity shared config
evidence: pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go:76 takes the namespace from the policy entry after variable substitution
pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go:83 resolver.Get(namespace, name) runs with no policy-namespace comparison
pkg/engine/context/resolvers/resolvers.go:41 the client resolver reads ConfigMaps in any namespace with Kyverno's credentials
pkg/validation/policy/validate.go:1404 requires only a non-empty namespace

traps.reason_to_dismiss: admission validation already rejects an empty configMap namespace (validate.go:1404), so the "default" fallback looks unreachable
evidence: pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap.go:80-82 replaces an empty substituted namespace with "default", not with the policy's namespace
pkg/validation/policy/validate.go:1404 checks the raw template string, so a `{{...}}` that substitutes to "" passes admission and reaches the fallback

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a namespace check at policy admission (validateAPICall) feels like the natural place for a static policy-authoring rule
evidence: pkg/engine/apicall/apiCall.go:61 substitutes variables into the whole APICall (including urlPath) only at runtime, so an admission-time check sees templates, not final paths

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a check that the path contains /namespaces/<policy-ns>/ looks sufficient
evidence: pkg/clients/dclient/client.go:168,170 RequestURI(path) forwards the path, query and dot-segments to the API server unchanged, so a lexical prefix/substring check can be fooled by: all-namespace list paths (no /namespaces/ segment), `<ns>-suffix` prefix collisions, `..` segments and query strings
pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go:46-47 any non-empty urlPath goes to the kube API, with GET or POST

These must keep working next to the hidden cross-namespace path: ClusterPolicy (empty namespace) must keep cluster-wide apiCall access; a namespaced policy must keep reading its own namespace's objects and plausibly the Namespace object /api/v1/namespaces/<own-ns> itself (that path has no trailing namespaced segment)
pkg/clients/dclient/client.go:170 POST through urlPath is supported, so a policy may legitimately POST to cluster-scoped review endpoints

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the cleanup controller is a separate component, its context only feeds deletion conditions, and it never shows up on the admission webhook path the report points at
evidence: pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller.go:173 calls ctxFactory(nil, kyvernov1.Rule{}) and passes a nil policy, so a factory-level check keyed on the policy's namespace treats a namespaced CleanupPolicy as cluster-scoped
pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller.go:174-181 loads spec.Context (apiCall/configMap entries) with c.client before any namespace scoping
pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller.go:187 the rest of the controller scopes by policy.GetNamespace(), showing the namespace is available here

traps.reason_to_dismiss: rule.Context is the documented place for context entries; nested foreach and mutate-target contexts look like the same feature
evidence: pkg/validation/policy/validate.go:1303 validateRuleContext walks only rule.Context, never ForEachMutation/ForEachValidation/ForEachGeneration.Context or ResourceSpec.Context
pkg/engine/handlers/mutation/common.go:97 and pkg/engine/handlers/mutation/mutate_existing.go:83 load nested contexts through the same loader at runtime

traps.reason_to_dismiss: GlobalContextEntry data is curated by a cluster admin and is meant to be shared, so reading it from a namespaced policy is arguably by design
evidence: pkg/engine/context/loaders/globalcontext.go:97 gctxStore.Get(gctxName) runs with no policy-namespace filter
pkg/cel/policies/vpol/compiler/compiler.go:254-256 the resource lib is namespace-scoped, while globalcontext.Lib at :242-244 takes no namespace

masking: T8 only shows up once a fix for T1/T3 is placed in the shared contextloaderfactory and keyed on the policy argument: the nil policy at cleanup/controller.go:173 then bypasses it silently

conflicts.what: a strict rule (path must start with /api(s)/.../namespaces/<own-ns>/, GET only) closes the path shapes in T6 but breaks reading the policy's own Namespace object and POSTs to cluster-scoped review endpoints
changing the "default" fallback for every policy instead of only namespaced ones changes behaviour that ClusterPolicy configMap entries rely on
treating a nil policy as forbidden (fail-closed) breaks ClusterCleanupPolicy context loading; the real fix is to pass the cleanup policy's namespace into the factory

fairness_risks: ClusterPolicy / ClusterCleanupPolicy (empty namespace) must keep unrestricted apiCall and configMap access (contextloaderfactory.go:20-21 shared by both)
Namespaced policies reading the policy's own Namespace object (/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>) is a common legitimate pattern, and a trailing-slash-only rule refuses it

Service apiCalls to genuine external services must keep working; tests for T2 should check only that Kyverno's SA token is not attached for namespaced policies (or that API-server targets are refused), not ban services
T10: blocking globalReference in namespaced policies may contradict the intended GlobalContextEntry sharing model; do not test it as a must-refuse

design.why: There are four independent fix sites, each with a different reason to dismiss: T1 is the advisory urlPath route, and its hidden tests should include the T6 path shapes and the T7 own-namespace/ClusterPolicy keep-working cases, which makes this group the mimo-type how/coupled-value test. T2 is deepseek-type: the service-call route that silently attaches Kyverno's token is easy to wave off as 'external SSRF'. T3 (with the T4 default-namespace fallback) is a second loader implementation (medium M2/M5). T8 is deepseek-type: the cleanup controller passes a nil policy, a wrong-object bypass that only matters once the obvious factory fix lands. T10 is left out because it is arguably by-design and carries a fairness risk. T5/T9 sit inside the T1 group, so they add no independent judgement.

unverified: Which route the published B fix (bbf3e5c01391) actually closed: I could not read the fix commits from the pinned tree. B is most likely T3 (configMap) or T2 (service call) given szz_status H3b-elsewhere, but this is unconfirmed

The A fix (e0ba4de4f1e0; eba60fa856c7) is absent from the pinned tree: there is no namespace check in pkg/engine/apicall or validateAPICall (validate.go:1411-1435). So whether A's code leaves B open, and whether A sits at admission or runtime, cannot be checked here
Whether GlobalContextEntry is cluster-scoped and admin-only (T10's reason to dismiss) was not checked against the CRD scope in api/
Whether the cleanup controller's client has broader read RBAC than the admission controller (T8's impact) was not checked in the charts
The CEL http lib (pkg/cel/libs/http) adds no SA token automatically (only test fixtures set Authorization), so it was not recorded as a route
